questions.question: Fitting a line through data points is described as solving a system of equations. What does the solution represent?
options: The raw data points themselves
The number of data points
The weights making predictions match observations
The error messages to display
questions.explanation: Fitting solves for weights. This lesson builds linear systems as the engine behind regression.

questions.question: Why does gaussian_elimination use partial pivoting on a column?
options: It makes every matrix positive definite
It swaps in the largest available absolute pivot to reduce numerical error
It removes the right-hand side from the augmented system
It guarantees a zero condition number
questions.explanation: Dividing by a tiny pivot amplifies rounding error. Choosing the largest available magnitude in that column is a simple stabilization step.

questions.question: When can the lesson's Cholesky routine factor a real symmetric matrix?
options: Whenever it has any negative diagonal entry
Only when it is rectangular
When it is positive definite, producing A=L L^T
When its determinant is exactly zero
questions.explanation: The diagonal update must stay positive. For a symmetric positive-definite matrix, the routine builds a lower triangular L whose product with its transpose reconstructs A.

questions.question: What system does least_squares_normal solve for an overdetermined design matrix A?
options: A A^T x = b
A x = A^T b without changing dimensions
A^T x = A b
A^T A x = A^T b
questions.explanation: Setting the gradient of ||Ax-b||^2 to zero gives the normal equations. The implementation forms AtA and Atb before solving.

questions.question: What does a very large condition_number(A) warn about?
options: Small input or rounding changes can cause large changes in the solution
A is guaranteed to have an exact integer solution
The matrix has more rows than columns
The residual must already be zero
questions.explanation: A large ratio of largest to smallest singular value indicates an ill-conditioned problem. Ridge regularization can improve stability by adding lambda I to A^T A.

questions.question: What does an augmented row [0, 0 | 1] reveal during elimination?
options: The system has a unique solution at the origin
The system is inconsistent because 0=1 cannot hold
The matrix has two independent pivots
The row should be treated as an extra free variable
questions.explanation: The coefficient row is zero but the right side is not. No vector can satisfy that equation, so the system has no solution.
